mainEntity.name: Who will I talk to?

acceptedAnswer.text: Someone from the KRIVA team is on the first call, the people who will ship the work, not a salesperson. The designers and engineers on the project join when scoping starts.

mainEntity.name: How old is the company?

acceptedAnswer.text: KRIVA Technologies was founded in 2025. Nine years refers to the team’s experience designing and shipping product software, not the age of the studio. We keep those two facts separate on purpose.

mainEntity.name: Where are you based, and how do time zones work?

acceptedAnswer.text: Headquarters is in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, India. The studio is remote-first. We overlap call hours with the US, UK, UAE, and Canada, deliver from Ahmedabad, and reply within one business day.

mainEntity.name: Do you subcontract?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Design and engineering stay in-house. If a project needs a specialist we do not have, we say so before we start rather than quietly farming the work out.

mainEntity.name: What services do you offer?

acceptedAnswer.text: We design and build trucking and logistics software, dispatch CRM, fleet dashboards, and driver apps, plus B2B SaaS ( onboarding, dashboards, MVPs ), QuickBooks and Xero integrations, and workflow automation . We focus on these areas because we have spent years on them.

mainEntity.name: Do you subcontract any work?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Every designer and engineer on your project is a permanent KRIVA team member. We do not use freelance marketplaces or offshore subcontractors. The team you meet on the first call is the team that builds your product.

mainEntity.name: Do you work with startups and enterprises?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both. For startups, we are used to fast timelines, limited scope, and investor-facing deliverables. For scale-ups and enterprises, we are used to compliance requirements, complex integrations, and multi-stakeholder sign-off. We scope projects accordingly.

mainEntity.name: Can you work with our existing team?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We embed with in-house designers, developers, or product managers and adapt to your tools and working style.

mainEntity.name: How long does a typical project take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A focused MVP or redesign is usually 6 to 10 weeks. A full-stack SaaS platform with integrations runs 12 to 20 weeks. Discovery sprints are 1 to 2 weeks. We give an honest timeline on the first call. See our delivery process for how phases and sign-off gates work.

mainEntity.name: How do you use AI in your delivery?

acceptedAnswer.text: We use Claude for content and brief drafting, GitHub Copilot for code generation, Cursor for rapid prototyping, and Figma AI for asset generation. Every output is reviewed by a senior team member before it reaches you. AI makes us faster; people make sure it is right.

mainEntity.name: Who owns the design files and code after the project?

acceptedAnswer.text: You do. All Figma files, GitHub repositories, and documentation transfer to you at project close, or earlier if you prefer. No lock-in or vendor dependency. We help onboard your internal team on what we built.

mainEntity.name: How is pricing structured?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fixed-scope projects, monthly retainers, or sprint-based work. Everything is scoped after discovery, with clear deliverables and milestones agreed upfront.

mainEntity.name: What happens after launch?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most clients move to a monthly retainer after go-live: iteration sprints, performance monitoring, and roadmap support. You can scale the retainer up or pause it as needed. We do not vanish after handoff.

mainEntity.name: Where are you based, and how do remote work and time zones work?

acceptedAnswer.text: Headquarters is in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, India. The studio is remote-first: we overlap call hours with the US, UK, UAE, and Canada, work async between those windows, and align stand-ups to your team’s schedule. In-person meetings are not required.

mainEntity.name: What do you need from us to get started?

acceptedAnswer.text: A brief ( we will send a template ), your timeline, and a 20-minute fit call. If you do not have a brief yet, we will write one together. Many clients arrive with a problem, not a spec.

mainEntity.name: Do you sign NDAs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Mutual NDAs are standard before we discuss sensitive product details or architecture.

mainEntity.name: How long does a typical project take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Discovery is 1–2 weeks. A full project is usually 6–16 weeks depending on scope. We will not quote a date until the brief is written. A fit call is for fit, not a fake timeline.

mainEntity.name: What do you need from us?

acceptedAnswer.text: A named decision-maker, access to the people who will use the product, and feedback inside the weekly cadence. If the desk cannot join a demo, we will say the engagement is not ready.

mainEntity.name: How do timezones work?

acceptedAnswer.text: We are remote-first from Ahmedabad, India, with overlap windows for UK and US clients. Demos sit in that overlap. Async notes go out the same day. You should not need midnight calls.

mainEntity.name: How is this different from AI-Assisted Development?

acceptedAnswer.text: This page is the delivery sequence: phases, gates, cadence. AI-Assisted Development is how we use Claude, Copilot, and Cursor inside those phases. Tools speed the work. A person still signs what ships.

mainEntity.name: Do QuickBooks and Xero projects use the same process?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Finance connectors still get a written brief, a signed operator surface, weekly demos, and a go-live checklist. The write into QuickBooks Online or Xero uses the original APIs. The gates do not change.

mainEntity.name: What happens after launch?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can take the handoff and run it, or stay on a monthly retainer for iteration and automation maintenance. Support is Phase 05 and optional. It is not bundled as a surprise.

mainEntity.name: Can Kriva redesign an existing mobile app?

mainEntity.name: Can the app connect with our existing platform or backend?

mainEntity.name: QuickBooks Desktop or QuickBooks Online?

acceptedAnswer.text: We primarily integrate QuickBooks Online via Intuit's API. Desktop is scoped case-by-case when the ledger cannot move to Online. Xero is always the cloud API.

mainEntity.name: Can you sync both Xero and QuickBooks for different regions?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Multi-region billing with separate connectors and a unified operator dashboard is a common SaaS pattern: QBO for US entities, Xero for UK, one exception queue.

mainEntity.name: How do you handle sync failures?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every job logs errors, retries with backoff and idempotency keys, and surfaces exceptions in an operator dashboard with a next step. Failures are visible before close, not after.

mainEntity.name: How is this different from Integrations & APIs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Integrations & APIs covers CRM, payments, ELD, and general connectors. This page is the finance-specific solution: QuickBooks, Xero, matching, close, and the operator UX around exceptions. Many products need both.

mainEntity.name: How long does a typical integration take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A focused QBO or Xero connector with operator UX is usually 8 to 12 weeks, including mapping sign-off and a parallel run. Dual-region or multi-entity setups run longer. We give a real range on the first call, not a padded one.

mainEntity.name: Stripe or payment processor sync?

acceptedAnswer.text: Payment events are source events in the same queue. Full payment connector scope lives under Integrations & APIs ; close UX and matching stay here.

mainEntity.name: Can you extend our existing TMS instead of replacing it?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, that's the most common path. We keep your TMS as the source of record and build dispatch consoles, driver apps, or portals beside it, connected through its API or database. Full replacement only comes up when the architecture itself is the constraint.

mainEntity.name: Can you replace spreadsheet-based dispatch workflows?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We map what the spreadsheet actually controls first, the queue, the SLA logic, the handoffs, then rebuild it as an audited board so nothing dispatch relies on gets lost in the transition.

mainEntity.name: Can a TMS be modernized without disrupting daily operations?

acceptedAnswer.text: That's the standard delivery model, not a special request. New surfaces run in parallel behind feature flags with sanitized staging data, and cutover happens in phases only after dispatch signs off. ShiftRail used staged go-live before full cutover.

mainEntity.name: Do you build individual modules or complete platforms?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both. Most engagements start with the highest-pain module, usually dispatch, and expand module by module in whatever sequence carries the least operational risk. A full platform is one possible endpoint, not the starting assumption.

mainEntity.name: What does the engineering stack look like?

acceptedAnswer.text: Next.js, React, and TypeScript, with integration tests against your TMS schema versions and sanitized staging data for dispatch-shaped QA. Dispatcher, supervisor, driver, carrier, and finance roles are modeled with the permissions each group actually needs.

mainEntity.name: What happens after launch?

acceptedAnswer.text: You own the source, designs, and documentation, retainer support is optional, with no lock-in. Iteration continues after go-live through operator feedback loops.

mainEntity.name: McLeod, TMW, or a proprietary TMS?

acceptedAnswer.text: We integrate via API, EDI, or file exchange, scoped in discovery, not assumed. See Integrations & APIs for connector architecture.
